The counterfactuals are clear: using a single cell with the substitute would take 35 hours and cost $3,115, saving only $87.50 while doubling elapsed production time; waiting for replenishment would cost no incremental amount but would finish in 83 hours, comprising 48 hours for replenishment plus 35 hours of production, and would miss the nearer 36-hour and 48-hour job deadlines. The split therefore buys a 17.5-hour schedule advantage over the single-cell substitute for a modest premium, and a 65.5-hour advantage over waiting. This assumes quantities reflect the current certificate, receiving and stock records, cell costs use the hourly rates in this snapshot, production can be split across compatible online cells, and substitute allocation draws only on verified available stock. The underlying gap remains unresolved: the certificate shows 120 units while receiving posted 80, so the held primary material is not issued under this option.
